_readme: THE BORE AT THE MOUTH (2026-10-26, Mark: "a rolling wave on the coast"). A 500 m impactor 800 km off the Merrimack (40.5 N 63 W;
a 1 km one there swung the sea side -110 to +130 m and swallowed the eye; Ward & Asphaug's 1950 DA stood at 35 N 70 W), the eye
to sea, 80 m up, from 16:45Z through the arrival at 30x. THE SHELF RUNG (section 6's rung 2): a second solver window over the
Gulf of Maine (`solvers`: 1600 x 1150 cells of ~260 m, the stack's coarse tier its bed, Boston's station its tide: the one near with a NAVD88 link) takes the
impact's level at its open sea by the same law and carries the train across the Gulf in nonlinear shallow water until its crests
shock; the Merrimack window's faces read the shelf's level (WaterManager::OwnedLevelAt), and the bore comes over the bar into the
standing water of the inlet. The bank kernel feeds its face to the crest law, the column plane folds where the labels overtake,
its whitewater is Belanger's. Without the shelf the train reached the window as kilometre-long gentle rises (2026-10-26).
